headline: Profit edges up year over year as trading activity cools
summary_short: CME Group's Q2 FY2026 revenue was $1.71B (+0.8% y/y, -9.2% q/q) and net income rose to $1,041.8M (+1.6% y/y); diluted EPS of $2.88 rose 2.5% y/y but fell 9.4% q/q as trading activity cooled from an unusually volatile first quarter.
summary_long: Revenue was $1.71B, up 0.8% y/y but down 9.2% q/q as market volatility eased from an unusually turbulent first quarter tied to early-2026 Middle East tensions. Clearing/transaction fees fell 3% y/y on a lower average rate per contract (more micro-contract mix, higher member trading), partly offset by an April 1 fee increase; market data revenue rose 20% y/y. Operating income fell to $1,107.1M (-2.0% y/y, -15.5% q/q) as salaries, tech-support, marketing, and stock comp expense rose. Net income was $1,041.8M (+1.6% y/y); diluted EPS $2.88 (+2.5% y/y). CME paid a $1.30/share dividend and repurchased $698M of stock; cash fell to $2.14B (-10.3% q/q). No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Revenue fell q/q as market volatility eased from an unusually turbulent first quarter; clearing and transaction fees fell on a lower average rate per contract (more micro-contract mix, higher member trading), partly offset by an April 1 fee increase and 20% y/y market data growth.

Operating income fell as higher salaries/headcount, technology-support costs (Google Cloud transformation), marketing, and stock-based compensation combined with the revenue decline; license fee expense also rose on record volumes in certain equity products.

Net income fell q/q on the sequential revenue decline and higher operating expenses, partly cushioned by higher non-operating income; y/y it rose slightly on modest revenue growth and higher S&P Dow Jones Indices equity earnings, despite lower OSTTRA contribution post-sale.

Diluted EPS fell q/q as net income declined on lower trading-driven revenue and higher operating expenses, but still rose y/y as revenue and non-operating income grew faster than the expense base and buybacks trimmed the share count.
Cash fell q/q mainly on $698M of share repurchases and continued dividend payments; the filing separately notes financing-activities cash use rose in the first half on increased share repurchases.

Management attributes relatively flat y/y Q2 volume to easing market volatility as the early-2026 Middle East-driven turbulence subsided; H1 volume had risen y/y on that same earlier volatility. No forward guidance was issued.
